nodes.title: Voice runtime audio path on the 4-vCPU sandbox: one runtime process holds about 25 concurrent phone calls before event-loop lag p99 passes 20 ms (12.8 ms at 25, 29.1 ms at 35); outbound audio stays on time to 35 calls and underruns at 50; one process is bound to one core (96% at 50); Silero VAD is the largest CPU cost (~24% of busy time), then numpy resampling and mu-law (~22%)
nodes.method: product/voice/bench/audio_bench.py --calls 10 25 35 50 --seconds 120 (metric as of fefbd7f), Python 3.13, Silero VAD, coding sandbox with 4 vCPU, 2026-10-21. Runtime in its own process; N Plivo-style mu-law 8 kHz media websockets over localhost through the real audio path (decode, 8->16 kHz FIR, Silero VAD, cascade turn-taking, reply door, 24->8 kHz FIR, encode, playAudio). Fake providers: final transcript +300 ms, first sentence +700 ms, first audio +250 ms then 2x real time. Callers: synthetic Azure TTS phone stimuli, ~2 s talk / 4-6 s quiet. n = outbound frames judged (26,354 + 65,485 + 91,478 + 128,747), after a 10 s warm-up. Results: N=10 cpu 32% (3.2%/call), RSS 175 MB, loop lag p50/p99/max 0.7/3.6/49.7 ms, frames >20 ms late 71 (0.27%), runtime turn-end->first-audio overhead p50/p99 176/204 ms (VAD end-of-speech 160 ms included). N=25 cpu 67%, 320 MB, lag 0.9/12.8/116.7, late 81 (0.12%), overhead 177/268. N=35 cpu 88%, 405 MB, lag 1.5/29.1/328, late 147 (0.16%), overhead 183/302. N=50 cpu 96%, 559 MB, lag 4.9/94.3/345.8, late p99 36.4 ms, 1,486 late (1.15%), overhead 209/484. Profile at N=30 (cProfile, 60 s): onnxruntime run 14.1 s of ~58 s busy; FIR correlate 3.4 s, ulaw_decode 3.5 s, downsampler 3.0 s, ulaw_encode 1.8 s; websocket parse/send ~4 s; reply-door regex 0.6 s. Load generator lag p99 1.4-1.7 ms (its numbers are trustworthy). Not measured: real providers, real carrier jitter buffers, the deploy host, more than one process.
nodes.value: ~25 calls per runtime process (one core) on the sandbox; RSS ~10 MB per call

nodes.title: Inference: calls per deploy host = processes x ~25 until measured there. Levers, by expected gain: one runtime process per core (4 vCPU -> ~100 calls); batch Silero VAD across calls into one onnx run; mu-law by lookup table and a cheaper 8<->16 kHz resampler; run the VAD only every second 32 ms window while the caller is silent
nodes.closes_when: audio_bench.py on the deploy host (and with real providers) gives the calls-per-process knee, and a multi-process run shows it scales with cores
